\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کاش} (kāsh)}{کاش (kāsh)}]{\ur{کاش} (kāsh) — if only; I wish}

\label{lesson:UR-C369-kash}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to get stuck, then the Urdu for to deal with.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کاش}}
\textbf{\ur{کاش}} — \emph{kāsh} — \textquotedblleft{}if only; I wish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کاش} \ur{میرے} \ur{پاس} \ur{وقت} \ur{ہوتا}!
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāsh mere pās vaqt hotā!}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If only I had the time!
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کاش}} (\emph{kāsh}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{kāsh}, \textquotedblleft{}would that\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāsh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāsh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāsh mere pās vaqt hotā!} — If only I had the time!
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to get stuck, then the Urdu for to deal with, then say \emph{kāsh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{کاش} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}If only; I wish\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ارمان} (armān)}{ارمان (armān)}]{\ur{ارمان} (armān) — a longing; a cherished wish}

\label{lesson:UR-C369-arman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to deal with, then the Urdu for if only.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ارمان}}
\textbf{\ur{ارمان}} — \emph{armān} — \textquotedblleft{}a longing; a cherished wish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{وہ} \ur{آتا} \ur{تو} \ur{میرا} \ur{ارمان} \ur{نکل} \ur{جاتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar voh ātā to merā armān nikal jātā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Masculine.

\textbf{\ur{ارمان}} (\emph{armān}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{armān}, \textquotedblleft{}a longing, a hope\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حسرت} (hasrat)}{حسرت (hasrat)}]{\ur{حسرت} (hasrat) — a wistful regret; an unfulfilled wish}

\label{lesson:UR-C369-hasrat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for if only, then the Urdu for a longing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حسرت}}
\textbf{\ur{حسرت}} — \emph{hasrat} — \textquotedblleft{}a wistful regret; an unfulfilled wish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{میں} \ur{پڑھتا} \ur{تو} \ur{آج} \ur{یہ} \ur{حسرت} \ur{نہ} \ur{ہوتی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar maiṅ paṛhtā to āj yih hasrat na hotī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If I had studied, I would not have this regret today.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حسرت}} (\emph{hasrat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥasra}, \textquotedblleft{}sorrow, regret\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ستانا} (satānā)}{ستانا (satānā)}]{\ur{ستانا} (satānā) — to pester; to torment}

\label{lesson:UR-C369-satana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a longing, then the Urdu for a wistful regret.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ستانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ستانا}} — \emph{satānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to pester; to torment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{بلی} \ur{کو} \ur{ستاؤ} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{وہ} \ur{کاٹے} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum billī ko satāo ge to voh kāṭe gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you pester the cat, she will bite.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بلی} \ur{کو} \ur{ستایا}, \emph{us ne billī ko satāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ستانا}} (\emph{satānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{satānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to persecute, to annoy\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{saṃtāpayati}, \textquotedblleft{}inflames\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12886).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{satānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum billī ko satāo ge to voh kāṭe gī.} — If you pester the cat, she will bite.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a longing, then the Urdu for a wistful regret, then say \emph{satānā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گنوانا} (ganvānā)}{گنوانا (ganvānā)}]{\ur{گنوانا} (ganvānā) — to waste; to throw away (time, a chance)}

\label{lesson:UR-C369-ganvana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a wistful regret, then the Urdu for to pester.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گنوانا}}
\textbf{\ur{گنوانا}} — \emph{ganvānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to waste; to throw away (time, a chance)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{وقت} \ur{نہ} \ur{گنواتے} \ur{تو} \ur{امتحان} \ur{پاس} \ur{کرتے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum vaqt na ganvāte to imtihān pās karte.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you had not wasted time, you would have passed the exam.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{وقت} \ur{گنوایا}, \emph{us ne vaqt ganvāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گنوانا}} (\emph{ganvānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{gãwānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to squander, to lose\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{gamáyati}, \textquotedblleft{}makes go\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4028).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ganvānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ganvānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum vaqt na ganvāte to imtihān pās karte.} — If you had not wasted time, you would have passed the exam.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a wistful regret, then the Urdu for to pester, then say \emph{ganvānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
